title: FlashAttention: Breaking the Quadratic Memory Wall

beats.text: Standard attention forces GPUs to materialize an N by N matrix, stalling memory pipelines when scaling context windows to hundreds of thousands of tokens.
beats.visual_focus: Grid visualization of an N by N attention score matrix overflowing VRAM capacity.

beats.text: Reading and writing intermediate attention scores between slow High Bandwidth Memory and chip compute units creates an inescapable memory-bound quadratic IO bottleneck.
beats.visual_focus: Chalkboard schematic showing high-latency data traffic between HBM memory and GPU SRAM compute blocks.

beats.text: FlashAttention eliminates large matrix materialization entirely by partitioning input sequences into compact blocks that fit inside fast on-chip SRAM caches.
beats.visual_focus: Tiled sub-matrices moving directly into fast on-chip SRAM without touching global DRAM.

beats.text: Using online softmax rescaling, the kernel computes attention incrementally in a single fused pass, scaling IO complexity strictly linearly with token length.
beats.visual_focus: Online softmax rescaling equation updating running maximum and sum across blocks seamlessly.

beats.text: This algebraic restructuring delivers a three to five times wall-clock speedup while reducing peak attention memory from quadratic down to linear.
beats.visual_focus: Split benchmark chart showing wall-clock execution time dropping sharply alongside memory consumption.

beats.text: Can hardware-aware algorithms unlock infinite context limits? Follow The Model Verse for the engineering behind modern AI architectures.
